Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 1:

Naming of the Surah

• It is called Al-Ahzab (The Confederates), because it mentions the confederate groups of the polytheists of Quraysh and those who allied with them: from Ghatafan, from Banu Qurayzah, and some of the Arabs, and their attack on Madinah. Allah repelled their scheming and spared the believers from fighting.

From the Objectives of the Surah

• Purifying the Islamic society from the remnants of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) by abolishing customs that had been inherited among them, such as adoption (tabanni), zihar (a pre-Islamic form of divorce by likening one's wife to one's mother), and their belief that a man of intellect has two hearts in his chest.

• Discussion of the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwat al-Ahzab), what it revealed of the hidden hypocrisy of the hypocrites (munafiqun), how the forces of evil and transgression banded together against the Muslims, and how Allah's mercy was manifested towards His allies by supporting them with troops from Him, fulfilling His promise of victory to them.

• Explanation of a number of rulings concerning the family system, such as some rulings related to women: the command to remain in their houses, to cover themselves and not display their adornment, the prohibition of speaking in a soft, seductive manner, the waiting period (iddah) of a divorced woman before consummation, the hijab, and others.

• Urging the believers to remember Allah and glorify Him, in gratitude for His guidance; the command to follow the Prophet (ﷺ) as an example; the magnification of his status with Allah and among the exalted assembly; and the command to send blessings and peace upon him.

• Warning the hypocrites and those who spread sedition that the Prophet (ﷺ) and the believers will be empowered against them, and discussion of the Hour and its horrors, and of the disbelievers and hypocrites as they taste the torment of Hell and burn in its blaze.

[Tafsir]

O Prophet, persist in piety towards Allah by acting on His commands and avoiding what He has forbidden, and let the believers take you as their model, for they are more in need of that than you are. And do not obey the disbelievers and the hypocrites. Indeed Allah is ever All-Knowing of everything, All-Wise in His creation, His command and His management.

Follow what is revealed to you from your Lord, from the Qur'an and the Sunnah (the Prophetic example and teachings). Indeed, Allah is fully aware of everything you do, and He will recompense you for it; nothing of that is hidden from Him.
And rely upon your Lord, entrust all your affairs to Him, and He is sufficient as a Guardian for whoever relies upon Him and turns back to Him.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 4:

Allah has not placed for any man two hearts within his chest. Nor has He made your wives whom you divorce by zihar (ﷺ) — in respect of prohibition — equal to the prohibition of your mothers. (Zihar is when a man says to his wife, "You are to me like the back of my mother." This used to be a form of divorce in the pre-Islamic era, so Allah clarified that a wife does not become a mother in any way.) Nor has Allah made the adopted children sons in the sharia. Rather, zihar and adoption have no reality in permanent prohibition. So the wife who has been subjected to zihar is not like the mother in prohibition, and lineage is not established by adoption through a person saying to the adopted child, "This is my son." That is merely words spoken by the mouth, having no reality and no legal weight. And Allah, glorified is He, speaks the truth and makes His way clear to His servants, and guides them to the path of rectitude.

Call them by their fathers' names; that is more just in the sight of Allah. But if you do not know their fathers, then they are your brothers in religion and your protégés in it. There is no sin upon you for the mistakes you make unintentionally; rather, Allah will hold you accountable for what you do deliberately. And Allah is ever Forgiving toward whoever errs, and Merciful toward whoever repents of his sin.

The Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) has a greater claim on the believers than they have on themselves, and he is closer to them than their own selves, in matters of religion and of worldly life. The sanctity of the wives of the Prophet (ﷺ) is for his community like the sanctity of their mothers, so it is not permissible to marry the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ) after him. Among the Muslims, those who are related by kinship have a greater right to the inheritance of one another, according to the judgment and legislation of God, than the inheritance through faith and emigration (hijrah). (In the early days of Islam, the Muslims used to inherit from one another through emigration and faith, not through kinship; then that ruling was abrogated (naskh) by the verses on inheritance.) Except that you, O Muslims, do a kindness to non-heirs by giving them support, goodness, maintenance, benevolence and bequest. This ruling mentioned was decreed and written in the Preserved Tablet (al-Lawh al-Mahfuz), so it is obligatory for you to act upon it. The verse indicates the obligation that the Prophet (ﷺ) be more beloved to the servant than his own self, and the obligation of complete submission to him. It also indicates the obligation to honour the Mothers of the Believers, his wives (ﷺ), and that whoever reviles them has indeed incurred loss.

And mention, O Prophet, when We took from the prophets their covenant, a firm pledge to convey the message, and We took a solemn covenant from you and from Noah, Abraham, Moses and Jesus, son of Mary (they are the Ulul-'Azm, the Messengers of firm resolve, according to the well-known view). We took from them a firm covenant to convey the message and to fulfil the trust, and that some of them would confirm one another.

God took that covenant from those messengers, so that He would question the messengers about what their nations answered them with. And He will reward the believers with Paradise, and He has prepared for the disbelievers on the Day of Resurrection a severe punishment in Hellfire.

O you who believe, remember the favour of God upon you when armies came against you, and We sent against them a fierce wind and hosts you did not see. And God is ever Seeing of what you do.

Wait, that is the Quranic verse, not the commentary. Here is the translation of the commentary as given:

O believers, remember the favour of God upon you in Medina during the day of the Battle of the Confederates (Ghazwat al-Ahzab), which is the Battle of the Trench (Ghazwat al-Khandaq), when the polytheists gathered against you from outside Medina, and the Jews and the hypocrites from within Medina and its surroundings, and they encircled you. So We sent against the confederates a fierce wind which uprooted their tents and overturned their cooking pots, and We sent angels from the heavens that you did not see, so terror fell into their hearts. And God is ever Seeing of what you do; nothing of that is hidden from Him.

This is the commentary on verse 10 of Surah al-Ahzab (33), as it appears in the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar:

"Remember when they came upon you from above you and from below you: from above you, from the upper part of the valley, from the direction of the east, and from below you, from the lower part of the valley, from the direction of the west. And remember when the eyes were fixed in bewilderment and astonishment from the intensity of the confusion, and the hearts reached the throats from the intensity of terror, and despair overcame the hypocrites, and rumors multiplied, and you harbored bad assumptions about Allah, that He would not support His religion nor raise His word."

In that terrifying situation the believers were tested and sifted, the true believer was distinguished from the hypocrite, and they were shaken with a severe trembling of fear and anxiety, so that their faith would become manifest and their certainty would increase.

And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is doubt, and who were weak in faith, said: "Allah and His Messenger promised us nothing but delusion!"

Wait, I should translate faithfully as it stands. Corrected version:

And when the hypocrites and those in whose hearts is doubt, and who were weak in faith, said: "What Allah and His Messenger promised us of victory and empowerment is nothing but falsehood of speech and delusion, so do not believe it."

And remember, O Prophet, the words of a group of the hypocrites, calling out to the believers of Madinah: "O people of Yathrib" (the old name of Madinah), "there is no place for you to stay in a losing battle, so return to your homes inside Madinah." Another group of the hypocrites asks the Messenger (ﷺ) for permission to return to their homes, on the pretext that they are unprotected, and so they fear for them. In truth they are not so, and they intended by this only to flee from the fighting.

If the armies of the confederates had entered Madinah from all its sides, and then these hypocrites had been asked to commit shirk against Allah and to abandon Islam, they would have answered that call eagerly, hastening to it, and they would have delayed in embracing shirk only briefly.

And indeed these hypocrites had made a covenant with Allah through His Messenger before the Battle of the Trench, that they would not flee when they witnessed battle, and would not hold back when called to jihad. But they broke their covenant. Allah will call them to account for that, and will question them about that covenant, and the covenant of Allah will be something they are held responsible for and answerable for.

Say, O Prophet, to these hypocrites: Fleeing from the battle out of fear of death or killing will not benefit you, for it does not postpone your appointed terms. And even if you flee, you will not enjoy this worldly life except for the limited span of your lives, which is a very brief period compared with the Hereafter.

Say, O Prophet, to them: "Who is it that can protect you from Allah, or shield you from His punishment, if He intends harm for you, or intends mercy for you?" Indeed, He is the Giver, the Withholder, the One who harms and the One who benefits. And these hypocrites will not find for themselves any guardian other than Allah who will befriend them, nor any helper who will support them.

God surely knows those who hold back others from fighting in the way of God, and who say to their brothers, "Come over to us, and leave Muhammad alone; do not fight alongside him, for we fear that you will be destroyed when he is destroyed." Yet even with their discouraging of others, they rarely come to the battle, and then only out of show and reputation-seeking, and fear of disgrace.

Stingy towards you, O believers, with wealth, lives, effort and affection, because of the enmity and malice in their hearts; out of love for life and dislike of death. So when fighting comes, they fear destruction, and you see them looking at you, their eyes rolling as though their minds have departed, out of fear of being killed and flight from it, like the rolling of the eyes of one who is facing death. But when the war is over and the terror has gone, they strike you with sharp, hurtful tongues. And when the spoils are divided, you find them stingy and envious. Those have not believed in their hearts, so Allah has nullified their deeds, and that is easy for Allah.

The hypocrites think that the confederates whom God has defeated with the worst defeat have not yet departed; that is because of their extreme fear and cowardice. Had the confederates returned to "Medina," those hypocrites would have wished that they were absent from "Medina," among the Bedouin nomads, asking about your news and inquiring about your reports from afar. And had they been among you, they would have fought with you only a little, because of their great cowardice, their abjectness, and the weakness of their certainty.

Indeed, there has been for you, O believers, in the sayings, deeds and circumstances of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) a good example for you to follow. So adhere to his Sunnah (the Prophetic way and practice), for only those who hope for Allah and the Last Day, and who remember Allah often, seek His forgiveness, and thank Him in every state, follow it and take him as their example.

When the believers saw the confederate forces (al-Ahzab) who had banded together around Medina and surrounded it, they remembered that the appointed time of victory had drawn near, and they said: "This is what Allah and His Messenger promised us: trial, tribulation, and then victory." So Allah fulfilled His promise, and His Messenger spoke the truth in what he had given them good news of. And seeing the confederates only increased them in faith in Allah, in submission to His decree, and in compliance with His command.

Among the believers are men who were true to their covenant with God, the Exalted. They endured patiently adversity and hardship and the time of battle. Among them are those who fulfilled their vow and were martyred in the way of God, or who died in truthfulness and faithfulness. And among them are those who await one of the two good outcomes: victory or martyrdom. They did not alter the covenant of God, nor did they break it or change it, unlike the hypocrites who altered it.

That is, that Allah may reward the people of truth for their truthfulness and their trials, and they are the believers, and He may punish the hypocrites if He wills to punish them, by not granting them repentance that is sincere before death, so they die in disbelief and deserve the Fire, or He may turn to them in mercy by granting them repentance and turning back to Him. Indeed Allah is ever Forgiving of the sins of those who transgress against themselves when they repent, and Merciful to them, since He has granted them sincere repentance.

God turned back the confederate forces of disbelief from "al-Madinah," frustrated, defeated and furious, having gained no good in this world or the next. God sufficed the believers in fighting by means of the causes He strengthened them with. God is All-Powerful, never overcome or subdued, and Mighty in His dominion and authority.

And Allah brought down the Jews of Banu Qurayza from their fortresses, because they had supported the confederates (al-Ahzab) in fighting the Muslims. He cast fear into their hearts, so they were defeated: you kill a group of them and take captive another group.

"And Allah gave you (O believers) their land, their dwellings and their wealth, movable such as ornaments, weapons and livestock, and immovable such as farmland, houses and strongholds that are impregnable, and He made you inherit a land you had not been able to tread before, because of its strength and its sanctity among its people. And Allah is ever Omnipotent over everything, nothing can overpower Him."

O Prophet, say to your wives, who have gathered around you seeking an increase in maintenance: If you desire the life of this world and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and release you in a fair manner, without harm or injury.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 29:

And if you desire God's pleasure and His Messenger's pleasure, and the abode of the Hereafter that God has prepared for you, then be patient with what you are in, and obey God and His Messenger. Indeed, God has prepared for the good-doers among you a great reward. (And they chose God and His Messenger, and what God has prepared for them in the Hereafter.)

O wives of the Prophet, whoever of you commits a clear act of disobedience, her punishment will be doubled twice over. Since their station is elevated, it was fitting that God make the punishment for the sin committed by them more severe, in order to safeguard their dignity and the dignity of the Messenger of God (ﷺ). And that punishment is easy for God.

Whoever of you (wives of the Prophet) obeys Allah and His Messenger, and does what Allah has commanded, We will give her the reward for her deed twice over the reward of other women among all women, and We have prepared for her a noble provision, which is Paradise.

O wives of the Prophet, you are not like any other women in merit and standing, if you fear Allah and obey His Messenger and keep away from what He has forbidden. So do not speak to strange men in a soft, tender voice that arouses desire in the one in whose heart there is immorality and sickness of forbidden lust. This is a duty of good conduct upon every woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day. And speak a word far from anything suspicious, one that the Sharia does not disapprove of.

Stay in your houses and do not go out except for a need, and do not display your adornments as the women of the former Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance before Islam) used to do. This is an address to the believing women in every age. And establish the prayer completely at its appointed times, O wives of the Prophet, and give the zakah as Allah has prescribed, and obey Allah and His Messenger in what they command and forbid. Indeed, Allah has enjoined upon you this, so that He may purify you, and remove from you the uncleanness and evil and wrong, O people of the house (ahl al-bayt) of the Prophet, which includes his wives and his descendants (peace and blessings of Allah be upon him), and purify your souls with the utmost purification.

And remember what is recited in your homes of the revelations of Allah and the wisdom (the Sunnah, the teachings of the Messenger (ﷺ)). Act upon them and hold them in the highest esteem, for they are among the blessings of Allah upon you. Indeed, Allah is Subtle and Gracious toward you, for He placed you in the homes in which the verses of Allah and the Sunnah are recited. And He is All-Aware of you, for He chose you to be wives of His Messenger (ﷺ).

Indeed, the men who submit to the commands of Allah and the women who do so, the believing men and the believing women, the obedient men to Allah and His Messenger and the obedient women, the truthful men in their words and deeds and the truthful women, the patient men who restrain themselves from desires, who persevere in acts of obedience, and who endure hardships, and the patient women, the men who fear Allah and the women who fear Him, the men who give charity, whether obligatory or voluntary, and the women who give charity, the men who fast, whether in obligatory or voluntary fasts, and the women who fast, the men who guard their private parts against unlawful intercourse and its preliminaries, and against exposing their nakedness, and the women who guard them, and the men who remember Allah often with their hearts and tongues and the women who remember Him: Allah has prepared for these forgiveness for their sins and a great reward, which is Paradise.

It is not fitting for a believing man or a believing woman, when Allah and His Messenger have decided a matter for them, that they should have any choice in their affair. And whoever disobeys Allah and His Messenger has certainly strayed into clear error.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 37:

And when you said, O Prophet, to the one on whom Allah had bestowed favour with Islam, and on whom you had bestowed favour with manumission, namely Zayd ibn Harithah, whom the Prophet (ﷺ) had freed and adopted: "Keep your wife Zaynab bint Jahsh and do not divorce her, and fear Allah, O Zayd." And you were concealing within yourself, O Prophet, what Allah had revealed to you concerning Zayd's divorce of his wife and your marriage to her. Allah is the One who will make manifest what you concealed. And you feared the hypocrites, lest they say: "Muhammad has married the divorced wife of his adopted son." Yet Allah has more right that you fear Him. So when Zayd had finished with her and divorced her, and her waiting period had ended, We married her to you, so that she would be an example in abolishing the custom of forbidding marriage to the wife of an adopted son after his divorce from her, and so that there would be no sin or blame upon the believers in marrying the wives of those whom they had adopted once those wives had been divorced and they had finished with them. And the command of Allah is always accomplished, with nothing to hinder or prevent it. The custom of adoption was practised in the Jahiliyyah, and it was then abolished by the words of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Call them by [the names of] their fathers﴾.

The Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 38:

There is no blame upon the Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ) for what Allah has made lawful for him, namely marrying the wife of the one he had adopted after she was divorced, just as He permitted this to the prophets before him. This is the way of Allah with those who passed away before, and the command of Allah is a decree determined, which must come to pass.

Then He, glory be to Him, mentioned the prophets who came before, and praised them by describing them as: those who convey the messages of Allah to the people, who fear Allah alone, and do not fear anyone other than Him. And Allah is sufficient as a Reckoner, calling His servants to account for all their deeds, and as an Observer of them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 40:

Muhammad ﷺ was not the father of any of your men, but he is the Messenger of Allah and the Seal of the Prophets (khatam al-nabiyyin), so there is no prophethood after him until the Day of Resurrection. And Allah has always been All-Knowing of everything you do; nothing is hidden from Him.

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted in accordance with His law: remember Allah with your hearts, your tongues and your limbs, a great deal of remembrance. Occupy your times with the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, at morning and evening, after the obligatory prayers, and at occurrences and circumstances. For this is a legislated worship that calls to the love of Allah, restrains the tongue from sins, and helps toward every good.

O you who have believed Allah and His Messenger and acted in accordance with His law: remember Allah with your hearts, your tongues and your limbs, a great deal of remembrance. Occupy your times with the remembrance of Allah, the Exalted, at morning and evening, after the obligatory prayers, and at occurrences and circumstances. For this is a legislated worship that calls to the love of Allah, restrains the tongue from sins, and helps toward every good.

This is a commentary passage on Surah al-Ahzab (33), verse 43. Here is the translation of the given text:

He is the One who showers His mercy upon you, and His angels pray for you, that He may bring you out of the darknesses of ignorance and misguidance into the light of Islam. And He is ever Merciful to the believers, in this world and in the Hereafter; He does not punish them as long as they remain obedient and sincere to Him.

The greeting these believers receive from Allah in Paradise on the day they meet Him will be "Peace," and it is a security for them from the punishment of Allah. He has prepared for them a good reward, which is Paradise.

O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness over your nation, testifying to their having been delivered the message; as a bringer of good tidings to the believers among them of mercy and Paradise; as a warner to the disobedient and the deniers of the Fire; as one who calls to the Oneness of Allah and to worshipping Him alone, by His command to you; and as a radiant lamp for whoever is illuminated by you. Your affair is manifest in the truth you brought, like the sun in its brightness and its shining; none denies it except a stubborn opponent.

O Prophet, indeed We have sent you as a witness over your nation, testifying to their having been delivered the message; as a bringer of good tidings to the believers among them of mercy and Paradise; as a warner to the disobedient and the deniers of the Fire; as one who calls to the Oneness of Allah and to worshipping Him alone, by His command to you; and as a radiant lamp for whoever is illuminated by you. Your affair is manifest in the truth you brought, like the sun in its brightness and its shining; none denies it except a stubborn opponent.
"And give good tidings, O Prophet, to the believers that they will have from Allah a great reward, which is gardens of Paradise."

Do not obey the disbelievers or the hypocrites, O Messenger, and disregard their harm. Let it not prevent you from conveying the message. Put your trust in Allah in all your affairs and rely upon Him, for He suffices you in everything that concerns you of the affairs of this world and the Hereafter.

O you who believe in Allah and His Messenger and act by His law: when you marry women and then divorce them before you have consummated the marriage with them, you have no waiting period (ʿiddah) for them that you need to count. So provide for them from your wealth a provision (mutʿah) by which they may benefit, according to your means, to console their hearts, and release them in a fair manner, without harm or injury.

O Prophet, indeed We have made lawful for you your wives whose bridal gifts (mahr) you have given, and We have made lawful for you what your right hand possesses of the captive women (ima') whom Allah has bestowed upon you. And We have made lawful for you the daughters of your paternal uncles and the daughters of your paternal aunts, and the daughters of your maternal uncles and the daughters of your maternal aunts, who emigrated with you. And We have made lawful for you a believing woman who gave herself to the Prophet without a bridal gift, if the Prophet wished to marry her, as a privilege exclusively for you and not for the believers. And there is no one other than you who may marry a woman by gift (hibah). We have indeed known what We have made obligatory upon the believers regarding their wives and their captive women: that they should not marry more than four wives, and as many captive women as they wish, and that the marriage be conditioned upon a guardian (wali), a bridal gift (mahr), and witnesses. But We have granted you a dispensation in what We made obligatory upon them, and We have extended to you what We did not extend to others, so that your heart would not be constricted in marrying those of these categories whom you married. And this is from the abundance of Allah's care for His Messenger (ﷺ) and His honoring of him. And Allah is ever Forgiving of the sins of His believing servants, Merciful in extending [allowances] to them.

This is the commentary of the King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 51:

You may defer whom you wish of your wives in turn of lodging, and take to yourself whom you wish of them. And whomever you seek from those whose turn you have deferred, there is no blame upon you in this. That choice is closer to their being pleased and not grieved, and to all of them being content with what you have apportioned to them. And Allah knows what is in the hearts of men of inclination toward some women over others. And Allah was ever Knowing of what is in the hearts, Forbearing, who does not hasten to punish those who disobey Him.

This is the commentary on Qur'an 33:52 from the King Fahd Complex's al-Tafsir al-Muyassar. It is not a Qur'anic quotation itself, so I translate the commentary text, rendering the verse's meaning in plain English within the explanation.

It is not lawful for you (O Messenger) to take women in marriage after your present wives, the Mothers of the Believers, nor to divorce them and exchange them for other wives—out of honour for them and in gratitude for their good conduct in choosing God, His Messenger and the Last Abode—even if the beauty of other women should please you, except those whom your right hand possesses of female slaves; they are lawful to you. And God is ever Watchful over everything, nothing of anything escapes His knowledge.

O you who have believed, do not enter the houses of the Prophet unless you are given permission for a meal, without waiting for its preparation. But when you are invited, then enter; and when you have eaten, disperse without lingering for conversation. Indeed, that lingering would hurt the Prophet, and he would feel shy to ask you to leave, but Allah is not shy of stating the truth. And when you ask the wives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) for something, such as utensils or the like, ask them from behind a screen. That is purer for your hearts and their hearts, away from the thoughts that occur to men regarding women and to women regarding men, for sight is the cause of temptation. It is not right for you to harm the Messenger of Allah, nor to marry his wives after his death, ever, because they are your mothers, and it is not lawful for a man to marry his mother. Indeed, harming the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and marrying his wives after him is a grave sin in the sight of Allah. This Ummah has complied with this command and avoided what Allah has forbidden in it.

If you reveal anything with your tongues, O people, of what harms the Messenger of Allah and what Allah has forbidden you, or if you conceal it within your souls, then indeed Allah, the Exalted, knows what is in your hearts and what you have made apparent, and He will recompense you for that.

No sin is upon the women for not veiling before their fathers, their sons, their brothers, their brothers' sons, their sisters' sons, the believing women, and the male slaves they own, because of the great need for them in service. And fear God, O women, that you do not transgress the limit set for you, so that you display of your adornment what you are not permitted to display, or abandon the veil before those from whom you are obligated to veil. Indeed, God is ever Witness over all things, Who sees the deeds of His servants, both inward and outward, and will recompense them for them.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 56:

Indeed, Allah praises the Prophet (ﷺ) before the angels brought near (to Him), and His angels pray for blessings upon the Prophet and supplicate for him. ﴿O you who have believed, send blessings upon him and greet him with peace.﴾ That is, those who affirmed Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: send blessings upon the Messenger of Allah and greet him with abundant peace, as a greeting and a magnification of him. The manner of sending blessings upon the Prophet (ﷺ) has been established in the Sunnah in various forms, among them: "O Allah, send blessings upon Muhammad and upon the family of Muhammad, as You sent blessings upon the family of Abraham; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious. O Allah, bless Muhammad and the family of Muhammad, as You blessed the family of Abraham; indeed You are Praiseworthy and Glorious."

Indeed, those who harm Allah, through polytheism or other sins, and those who harm the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) through words or deeds, Allah has cast them away and banished them from every good in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them in the Hereafter a punishment that will humiliate and debase them.

Those who harm believing men and believing women, by word or deed, without any wrong they have committed, have certainly borne a grave slander and a manifest sin, deserving punishment in the Hereafter.

O Prophet, say to your wives, your daughters, and the wives of the believers: let them draw their outer garments (jalabib) down over their heads and their faces, to cover their faces, their chests and their heads. That is more fitting that they be recognized by their covering and modesty, so that no one harms them or troubles them. And Allah is ever Forgiving and Merciful, for He has forgiven you what has passed and has shown mercy to you by making clear to you what is lawful and what is unlawful.

If the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is disease, and those who spread false rumours in the city of the Messenger (ﷺ) about [the believers'] shameful deeds and evils do not desist, We will surely set you (ﷺ) over them, and then they will not remain with you in it except for a little while. Cursed and expelled from the mercy of Allah, wherever they are found they will be seized and slain with a thorough slaying, for as long as they persist in hypocrisy and in spreading false rumours among the Muslims with the aim of sedition and corruption.

If the hypocrites, those in whose hearts is disease, and those who spread false rumours in the city of the Messenger (ﷺ) about [the believers'] shameful deeds and evils do not desist, We will surely set you (ﷺ) over them, and then they will not remain with you in it except for a little while. Cursed and expelled from the mercy of Allah, wherever they are found they will be seized and slain with a thorough slaying, for as long as they persist in hypocrisy and in spreading false rumours among the Muslims with the aim of sedition and corruption.

Here is the translation of the passage:

This is the way of Allah (sunnat Allah) and His course of action concerning the hypocrites of earlier nations: they are to be seized and killed wherever they are found. And you will not find, O Prophet, any alteration or change in the way of Allah.

The people ask you, O Messenger, about the time of the Hour, deeming it far-fetched and denying it. Say to them: The knowledge of the Hour is only with Allah. And what would make you know, O Messenger, that perhaps its time is near?

God has cast the disbelievers out of His mercy in this world and the Hereafter, and has prepared for them in the Hereafter a Fire, blazing and intensely hot, in which they will remain forever. They will find no protector to take charge of them and defend them, nor any helper to support them and rescue them from the Fire. On the Day when their faces are turned over in the Fire, they will say, regretful and bewildered: "Would that we had obeyed God and obeyed His Messenger in the world, so that we would have been among the people of Paradise."

The Disbelievers will say on the Day of Resurrection: "Our Lord, we obeyed our leaders in misguidance and our chiefs in polytheism, and they led us astray from the path of guidance and faith. Our Lord, give them double the punishment of our punishment with which we are punished, and cast them away from Your mercy with a severe casting away."

And in this is evidence that obeying other than Allah in opposing His command and the command of His Messenger brings upon oneself the wrath and punishment of Allah, and that the follower and the one followed are equal partners in the punishment. So let the Muslim beware of that.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law, do not harm the Messenger of Allah by word or deed, and do not be like those who harmed Prophet Musa (Moses), whereupon Allah cleared him of what they said about him of lies and falsehood, and he was, in the sight of Allah, of great standing and rank.

O you who have believed in Allah and His Messenger and acted by His law: act in obedience to Him, and avoid His disobedience, lest you thereby deserve punishment. And speak, in all your circumstances and affairs, words that are upright and correct, agreeing with what is right and free of falsehood and vanity.

If you fear Allah and speak words that are upright and on target, He will set right your deeds for you and forgive you your sins. Whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger in what He commands and forbids has indeed attained the greatest honor, in this world and in the Hereafter.

We offered the trust (al-amanah), which Allah entrusted to the accountable people, namely carrying out His commands and avoiding His prohibitions, to the heavens, the earth and the mountains. They refused to bear it and feared that they would not be able to fulfill it. Man bore it and took it on, despite his weakness. Indeed, he was greatly unjust to himself and ignorant of its consequences.

Commentary of King Fahd Complex (al-Tafsir al-Muyassar) on surah 33, verse 73:

So that Allah may punish the hypocritical men who show Islam while concealing disbelief, and the hypocritical women, and the polytheistic men who associate others with Allah in worship, and the polytheistic women, and that Allah may accept the repentance of the believing men and the believing women by covering over their sins and forgoing their punishment. And Allah is ever Forgiving to His servants who repent, and Merciful to them.
